# Questions waiting for your decision

> English rendering of [OPEN-QUESTIONS.md](OPEN-QUESTIONS.md). The Azerbaijani file is the source: numbering and sections are the same, and when the two differ, the Azerbaijani file wins. Update both together.

Everything else is ready and runs locally. The items below need either an external account or key, or a business decision.

## Keys and providers
1. **Anthropic API key and model.** Without `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` the AI tutor answers from the lesson text, and the Studio draft says "AI is not connected". The tutor has its own model: `ANTHROPIC_TUTOR_MODEL` (default `claude-haiku-5-5`). The Studio draft uses `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` (default `claude-opus-5-5`); to save cost, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL=claude-haiku-5-5` also works there. Which one? **2026-11-04:** the AI subtitles in the lesson player (65 languages outside the ten, ADR-029) also use this key and `ANTHROPIC_TUTOR_MODEL`. Without the key the player still offers those languages but says "No subtitles in this language for this lesson"; a live test has to wait for the key.
2. **Voice (TTS).** The pipeline is ready (ADR-028): ElevenLabs `eleven_v3` clips with word timings for every sentence, and the browser's speech synthesis where there is no clip. No clips have been generated yet; two things are needed:
   - `ELEVENLABS_API_KEY` (only in `.env.local`, for the script) and a choice of plan. All ten languages come to about 4 million characters, about USD 321 (2026-11-04 `--dry-run`; USD 26–38 per language).
   - A voice per language: `ELEVENLABS_VOICE_<LANG>`. ElevenLabs retires its default voices on 2026-12-31, so a native speaker of each language must pick its voice from the Voice Library and listen to one sample lesson (az, ka and ar especially). Who will choose?
3. **SMTP.** Without SMTP, invitations, reminders and report emails stay in the "logged" state (Settings → Email → Log). Which server?
4. **SMS/voice provider.** The `SMS_PROVIDER=webhook` interface exists; a real provider (for example Twilio or a local operator's gateway) and a sender name are needed.
5. **Email for demo requests.** `SALES_EMAIL`: requests are always stored in the operator console; if you wish, they can also arrive by email.

For believability at the address level (for example `ofistechizat-az.com`), a separate simulation sender domain with its SPF/DKIM setup is needed. Which domain(s)?
19. **CMS for the public site (operator console).** In the original, the landing texts, images and audio clips were edited from the operator console (publish / revert / reset). The content now lives in `content/landing/*.json` files; an operator UI can be added in a later phase. Is it needed?
20. **The AI provider in the legal texts (legal review needed).** The Privacy Policy (5.1, 6, 7.2) and Terms of Use (10.1) name Google Cloud Vertex AI for AI Sel's answers, left over from the original Cylosof text. In this portal AI Sel works through the Anthropic Claude API (ADR-008), and spoken questions are turned into text by the browser's speech recognition (a Google service in Chrome). With a lawyer, the text must be aligned with the real providers (Anthropic, cross-border transfer, retention period); we do not change the text without your approval. **2026-11-04:** the Vertex AI name is now in all ten languages of the legal texts (20 files: `privacy.*.md`, `terms.*.md`), so each of them needs the correction. The AI subtitles (ADR-029) also send lesson text to Anthropic, and ElevenLabs receives lesson text only when clips are generated (ADR-028); both must appear in the text.
21. **New mascot: duck or cat.** Two designs were made: a white duck (`design/mascot-duck/`, an interactive page) and a white-grey cat that resembles your cat (`design/mascot-cat/`). Both are built to the portal's mascot API (mood, gesture, speaking, gaze, touch, still mode). The mascot you choose will be connected to the portal as a component in place of the Rive file; the name AI Sel stays. Which one? **2026-10-21:** the cat was connected everywhere for you to look at (ADR-022); if it is not kept, the Rive robot returns with one line. **2026-11-04:** the cat received a new storybook drawing, many acts and the "Play with Sel" card on the Home page (ADR-031). Going back to Rive is now a little more than one line: the Rive wrapper must also accept the `auto` and `onCat` props, or they must be removed from the call sites.

## Left over from the 2026-11-04 release
22. **Open terminology choices (tr, ro, uk).** The editors chose these, but without native human confirmation (the "Reviewer notes" of the glossaries, `.claude/skills/cyclowareness-experience/references/glossaries/`):
   - tr: "oltalama" (USOM) was kept, not Microsoft's "kimlik avı"; "QR kod" was kept, not the official "karekod"; the current wording of the Cyber Security Directorate / USOM and the name of the streak freeze were not checked online.
   - ro: in Moldova "Confidențial" can read as a state-secret classification, so if the market includes Moldova a corporate alternative is needed; Romanian voices read "Elchin" as "Elkin", so before narration a phonetic spelling in the `spoken` field ("Elcin", "Rașad") or a TTS dictionary is needed; "AI" was kept, not "IA".
   - uk: no official source was found for "вішинг"; "інфостилер" was kept (CERT-UA writes "стілер / програма-викрадач"; the explanation was kept); "двоетапна" is the normative form, while Google writes "двохетапна".
   Should these choices stay, or should a native editor decide?
23. **Open items from the security audit (ADR-033).** **2026-11-05:** (a) and (b) are closed (ADR-041: Server Actions at 1 MB, the sandbox on its own route, SSO `sub` binding); (c) remains. (a) The 11 MB body limit of Server Actions applies to every action, including public actions without sign-in; the sandbox upload can move to its own route and the limit be reduced. (b) An SSO account is found by email only; binding the IdP's `sub` value to the account should be done together with the SSO test (question 14). (c) This computer runs Node 24.18.0; the Brotli CVE needs 24.22.1 or later: you need to update Node (the Docker image gets a new Node with `--pull`).
24. **Codex CLI crashes on this computer.** 0.164 crashed with 0xC0000005; after the update to 0.166 even `codex doctor` crashes with code 139, so the Codex/Claudex Loop reviews were replaced by ECC and agent-skills reviewers. If Codex is needed, try it on another machine or a new version; otherwise this path is closed.
25. **Lesson completion is not verified on the server.** ✅ Resolved (2026-11-05, ADR-035): the start time, the furthest scene, a minimum duration and answers scored on the server are checked; the parameters are in question 27. `completeLessonAction` does not check that the lesson's scenes were really passed; the furthest scene reached (`maxIndex`) is only in the browser (ADR-030). A learner who knows the browser tools can submit a lesson as "completed" without watching it. If the certificate and the compliance report are used as evidence, should we add a short check on the server (start time, minimum duration, number of answers)?

Rows written by the seed and the live drill count as `server_verified` (they are server-internal); do you want a separate `seeded` kind? Until confirmed, these values apply. A real browser test of the player has not been done yet (PROGRESS, "Not yet verified").
28. **Demo password and the presentation copy on port 3100 (ADR-036).** The seed no longer uses a published password: if `SEED_PASSWORD` is empty, the seed generates a random password and prints it only once, at the end. If you want a fixed demo password, write your own `SEED_PASSWORD` (at least 12 characters) into `portal/.env.local` on the presenting machine. The presentation copy on 3100 was seeded with the old, published password: re-seed it with your own password (`--reset`) or change the accounts' passwords, and check the audit log for sign-ins you do not recognise. The new `0003_wave_a` migration cannot create its unique indexes on a database with duplicate attestations or module/path certificates: if the old copy is not migrated, `--reset` solves this too. A local `npm run e2e` also needs `SEED_PASSWORD` in the environment or in `.env.local` (`.env.example` is empty now). Until this is done, the copy is open with a publicly known password.

Start the copy from a terminal: `npm --prefix portal run demo -- --port 3100` (add `--prod` for a production build, `--reset` for a fresh organisation). ## Left for the owner from the 2026-11-06 closing round (wave B)
42. **Password re-entry and support access (ADR-044).** **2026-11-10:** the Support access text now says password reset link in ten languages (ADR-068); the other questions stay open. A 2FA reset, a reset link, a role change and an operator link ask for the actor's own password; the limit is 10 per 15 minutes per actor, and successful attempts count too: an administrator who changes the role of 11 people within 15 minutes gets `rateLimited` even with the right password (the password confirmation in the profile works the same way). The target and the actor do not receive the colleague notice. A second approver (four-eyes) was not built. The support window is one 72-hour window per organisation, not per administrator. If the organisation's SMTP is switched off, the reset email goes through the platform transport or to the log (like the other fixed notices). The "Support access" text in Settings says the operator creates a "one-time sign-in link"; in fact it is a password reset link. From you: should successful step-ups count towards the limit (or should we add a read-only check to `rate-limit.ts` and count only failures, with the profile limit the same way); should the actor also receive the colleague notice; which customer needs a second approver (who approves, and what happens when there is only one administrator); should the window's length and scope stay; should the support text be corrected to "password reset link" in all ten languages?
43. **Rotating APP_SECRET (ADR-045).** The runbook (`docs/OPERATIONS.md`, "Rotating APP_SECRET") says to create and store the new key, deploy with both keys, run `scripts/rotate-secret.ts` and remove the old key; the code sets no rotation schedule, and the runbook is called from the "Contain" step of incident response. Backup codes issued before the rotation work only while `APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS` stays set, and stop at step 4 (the runbook tells administrators to ask people to renew their codes). On an installation with a verified domain, `APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET` must be set before the first rotation, equal to the `APP_SECRET` that was in use when the TXT records were published (otherwise the script refuses). The runtime image has no tsx: the script is run from a checkout of the deployed version or with the compose `seed` service; it has not been tried in the image. From you: where is the previous key kept during a rotation, and for how long (storing `APP_SECRET` is question 33); when is rotation done (only after an incident, or on a schedule, and by whom); is it acceptable that old backup codes stop working, or should the previous key be kept longer; should `APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET` be set in production now? Reviewer note: `kid` is a sha256 without a purpose label; if you want to change that, say so before the first v2 values are created in production.
44. **One verified domain and the `0004_wave_b` migration (ADR-045).** `tenants_domain_verified_idx` cannot be created in a database where two organisations already have the same verified domain, and the whole migration (`migrate.mjs` at container start) stops. The seed verifies only the demo organisation's domain, so the local and compose seeds are not affected. From you: before the deploy, does `select domain, count(*) from tenants where domain_verified_at is not null group by domain having count(*) > 1` return nothing on the production database? If it returns rows, an `UPDATE` that clears `domain_verified_at` on every row except the oldest for each domain must run before the migration: tell us which organisation keeps the domain.
45. **Row-level security (RLS) in the database (ADR-046, S-03).** Decision: not built now. Isolation between organisations lives in application filters, and `tests/cross-tenant.test.ts` checks every server action and API method (159 entries) with another organisation's ids and a lower role, and found no leak; a new entry cannot be merged without a row. RLS is XL work: a transaction and `SET LOCAL` per request (the `db()` singleton changes), a non-owner application role in compose, `tenant_id` on about 12 child tables, and a bypass for the operator and the job runner. From you: do bank and government buyers require database-level isolation by contract, or is the automated suite enough for due diligence? If a customer requires it, RLS goes on the roadmap. The RLS claim in privacy §9 is a separate item, question 26 (removed in wave C, ADR-067).
46. **Tutor cache per organisation (ADR-046, S-10).** In library lessons, AI Sel's answer is no longer given to another organisation: each organisation makes its own request to Anthropic for the first answer to the same question (more calls). Old `tutor_cache` rows whose keys have no organisation stay orphaned until the 365-day cleanup. From you: is the extra cost acceptable, or should answers be moderated and shared across organisations? Should we free the space at once with a one-off `delete from tutor_cache` during the deploy?
47. **Simulation sender and DNS (ADR-047, follow-up to question 18).** A simulation email is sent from a look-alike address only after the organisation publishes the Domain proof TXT record on that domain. The proof is one-off: there is no daily re-check and no grace period, so if the domain expires and passes to someone else, simulations keep going out with that From (replies and bounces reach the new owner); the guide tells the administrator to remove the address in that case. The beacon step shows a short blank page before the fake sign-in. The Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace sections (3 and 4) of `docs/SIMULATION-DELIVERY.md` were written without being checked on a live tenant. Base images are now pinned by digest and Node updates come through Dependabot; the sentence "a new Node with `--pull`" in question 23 (c) is out of date. From you: which look-alike domain(s) are registered for each customer, and who sets up their SPF/DKIM/DMARC records at the SMTP provider; someone who runs a real M365/Workspace tenant should read sections 3 and 4 of the guide once; should the look-alike domain's proof also be checked daily with a 7-day grace period, like the organisation domain (two new settings and a second loop in the job runner)?
48. **Retention defaults and residency (ADR-048, L-03).** **2026-11-10:** the minimum is now in the code (ADR-055): `auditMonths` is 0 or at least 12, and `settings.retention` and `retention.purged` entries are never deleted; the default and the other questions stay open. The default is "keep everything" (0/0): nothing is deleted until an administrator chooses. `auditMonths` had no minimum: choosing 1 month deleted the audit history after one month, including the records of the change itself. Only closed risks are deleted, by their closing date; open risks stay (deleting all of them is one line in `jobs.ts`). Demo requests are deleted after 730 days (question 34). The hosting region in `docs/OPERATIONS.md` is a placeholder (`<hosting region, open question for the owner>`); the region is question 12. From you: should the default stay "keep everything"; is the 12-month minimum right; is keeping open risks right; where was the "24 months for demo requests" promise published, so that the text can match what the system does; in which region does the data stay?
49. **Limits of the SCORM 1.2 package (ADR-049, answer to question 11).** A module is exported as a SCORM 1.2 zip (Studio → "Export for LMS"); there is no xAPI. The package sends nothing back to the portal: completion, score and time stay in the LMS and do not change the portal's progress, XP, risk or certificates. The mastery score is 80 for every package. The package has no tutor, the voice is Web Speech (no ElevenLabs clips), and the lessons are in one language. SCORM 1.2's 4,096-character `suspend_data` limit fills up in a module of about 200 lessons. The package has not been tried in any real LMS (SCORM Cloud, Moodle and so on), and `launcher.html` has not been opened in a browser from `file://`. From you: should the mastery score be chosen per module or per export; should LMS completions flow back into the portal's progress (that means an API from the LMS to the portal); in which LMS will the package be tried, and by whom (which LMS does the first pilot use)?
50. **Limits of the risk story (ADR-050).** The story shows an empty state when there are fewer than 7 snapshot days, a department can be named "most exposed" only with at least 3 members, and the window is 21 days. These are constants in `risk-story.ts`, not organisation settings. The section in the compliance pack ignores the pack's period and carries the date of the day it is printed. The texts were translated into ten languages by AI agents (the German `training` sentence's singular form was fixed on 2026-11-10, ADR-068). From you: do these limits suit your customers, or should they be organisation settings; should the section be left out entirely of a pack printed for a past period?
51. **Seat count and billing (ADR-051, together with question 13).** A seat is an active user who is not an operator; invited people are a separate column in the export, and suspended people are not counted. For pilots, billing is done by hand from the `/api/super/seats` CSV; there is no trial period and no self-service payment. A person can belong to one organisation; a membership model is planned for after the pilots (D-05). From you: should invited people count as paid seats; should suspended people count at all?
52. **Language of the engineering documents and the customer documents (O-02, O-05).** `DECISIONS.md` starts with an English index, and `OPEN-QUESTIONS.en.md` is the English mirror of items 1 to 65; the Azerbaijani text is the source and wins when they differ. For every new ADR and question, the index row and the mirror must be updated too. `docs/ADMIN-GUIDE.md` and `docs/LEARNER-QUICKSTART.md` were checked against the code from before wave B (1a45970); `docs/SECURITY-WHITEPAPER.md` was updated after wave B: password re-entry, key rotation and retention are now described there with their limits (ADR-044, 045, 048), the key rotation and password re-entry bullets were removed from its "does not provide yet" list, and the retention bullet was narrowed to data residency only (the other bullets of the list remain); sections 5, 14 and 17 of `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` have been out of date since wave A. The text of the report email in ten languages was written by an AI agent. From you: should the documents stay bilingual (Azerbaijani source, English mirror), or be English only; who does the legal review of the whitepaper and the admin guide before they go to customers, and can the "does not provide yet" list be published as it is; give the texts for the SLA, support hours, status page and the vulnerability reporting address (question 36).

## Left for the owner from the 2026-11-10 security audit (ADR-052)
53. **Production over plain HTTP (ADR-052, rejected item a).** `ALLOW_HTTP_APP_URL=1` lets production accept an `http://` `APP_URL`; `env.ts` and `.env.example` describe the flag as being for an intranet or a local test stack. The session and SSO cookies, however, get the `__Host-` prefix and the `Secure` flag from `NODE_ENV` alone (`auth/session.ts`, `auth/oidc.ts`, `proxy.ts`): over plain HTTP the browser discards them, and sign-in and SSO do not complete. HSTS and `upgrade-insecure-requests` follow the scheme of `APP_URL` and are not sent over plain HTTP. The audit rejected this as intended behaviour. Deployment is your decision (hosting is question 12). From you: will production, intranet installations included, always be served over HTTPS, or do you accept that sign-in fails over plain HTTP?
54. **Idle timeout for administrators (ADR-033, ADR-052).** A session lasts 30 days and is extended while it is used, but ends at the latest 90 days after sign-in (`SESSION_DAYS`, `SESSION_MAX_DAYS`, `auth/session.ts`). There is no shorter idle timeout, not for administrators either, and an organisation cannot set one. The audit recorded this as a design choice, not a finding; a bank buyer may ask for it. It is a choice between the administrators' convenience and the buyers' requirements. From you: do administrators need a shorter idle timeout, for example sign-out after 30 minutes without activity?
55. **SVG logos with embedded rasters or from old Illustrator versions (ADR-056).** The SVG logo check refuses when in doubt. The deliberate refusals include raster images embedded as `data:` URIs (Figma image fills, bitmaps embedded by Illustrator and Inkscape) and Illustrator 10 to CS3 "Save As SVG" and "Preserve Illustrator editing capabilities" exports (an internal DTD subset with `ns_svg`/`ns_ai` entities); the full list is in point 5 of ADR-056. On a refusal the administrator sees a general message: it names a script, an event attribute or a reference outside the file and suggests uploading a PNG, while for these files the reason is different. PNG and JPEG logos up to 512 KB are accepted. Accepting rasters in `<image>` means new code and a decoder-level check; the PNG path works today. From you: should `data:image/png` and `data:image/jpeg` be accepted in `<image>` (with a decoder-level check), or should administrators be told to upload a PNG for such logos?
56. **An author approving their own Studio material (ADR-052, rejected item b).** The approval gate (`decideMaterialAction`, `actions/secops.ts`) does not compare the author with the approver: analysts and administrators hold both `studio.write` and `approvals.decide`, so they can approve their own material. For a material that needs two approvals, the second approver must differ from the first (`sameApprover`), but the author can be the first approver. The audit rejected this as intended for small organisations, where there may be no other approver. Separation of duties is the customer's control policy, so the decision is yours (a second approver for administrator actions is question 42). From you: should this stay, or should a material require a second approver other than its author?
57. **The open-tracking pixel and mail scanners (ADR-052, rejected item e; ADR-047).** The open pixel (`/api/t/<token>/open`) records an open for every well-formed token and does not filter mail scanners (only a cancelled campaign records nothing), while clicks and fake sign-ins go through the scanner filter. Image proxies (Gmail, Apple Mail Privacy Protection) and scanners open every image, so opens appear in the campaign funnel and the report, but carry no risk score (`docs/SIMULATION-DELIVERY.md`, section 6). The audit rejected this as intended behaviour. How open figures are presented to customers is your decision. From you: do you confirm that opens stay informational only (outside the risk score and the evidence)?

## Left for the owner from the 2026-11-10 closing round (wave C)
58. **Load-test scale (ADR-060).** Risk scores are written in batches of 500 people, reminders, manager alerts and refreshers run at most once an hour per organisation, and a campaign launch writes its recipients and their emails in batches of 500. `portal/load/launch.js` is a k6 scenario: ten administrators launch a campaign at the same moment while `/api/health` is polled for 15 minutes; the thresholds are under 30 s for every launch and under 1 s for the health p95. The script has not been run: it needs a PostgreSQL staging copy with 10 organisations of 5,000 people (hosting is question 12). Timing change: reminders, manager alerts and refreshers can now go out up to 59 minutes later; when an assignment change touches more than 2,000 people, the new scores appear on the next tick (about a minute later), not within the request. From you: what scale (organisations × learners) should the load test target, and who runs it on which staging copy; are delays of up to 59 minutes acceptable?
59. **Where profile photos are stored (ADR-061).** A profile photo no longer travels as a data URL with the session query and the pages: the browser gets it only from `GET /api/avatar/[userId]` (only for a signed-in person, only for an id in their own organisation, `cache-control: private, max-age=3600`). The photos themselves are still stored in the database as data URLs in the `users.avatar_url` column; no object storage is configured. The cat mascot's engine now loads late as a separate chunk; whether it loads under the CSP of the presentation copy on 3100 has not been checked (we do not touch that copy). From you: should the photos move to object storage (which provider, together with hosting, question 12), or stay in the database; when you rebuild the presentation copy, check that the cat appears.
60. **Reporting API tokens: whose identity, `audit.read` and the plan (ADR-064).** A token acts as the administrator who created it, limited to the token's permissions: when the creator is suspended the token gets 401, when the creator is deleted the token is deleted too, and when the creator's role loses a permission the token loses it too. The brief asked for the "never a session user" model; this difference waits for your decision. `audit.read` is in the schema but has no endpoint, and it is hidden from the minting form until one exists (existing tokens still list it). Tokens need the `integrations` plan feature: the Essentials plan cannot mint tokens, after a downgrade a token gets 403, and revoking still works. From you: is it acceptable for banks that a token stays bound to the administrator who created it (the integration stops when that person leaves), or should a tenant-level service identity be built; should an audit-log export (CSV) be built for `audit.read`, or should the permission leave the schema; should tokens stay limited to plans with `integrations`?
61. **Report address: mail provider and forged From (ADR-065).** The organisation's mail provider posts every message that reaches the report address as generic JSON to `POST /api/inbound/{slug}`, with the organisation's bearer secret. Only this generic format is built: Mailgun, Amazon SES and Postmark need a small adapter in front. The secret proves that the request comes from the provider, not who wrote the mail: if the provider does not check it, a forged `From` can be filed as a report in another person's name. `docs/API.md` (section 10) tells administrators to have the provider reject mail that fails SPF, DKIM or DMARC; a check of the provider's signature (Mailgun or Postmark HMAC) is not built and depends on the choice of provider. The Outlook add-in (the large alternative in M-06) is not built. From you: which mail provider (Mailgun, SES, Postmark or an M365 connector), report address and MX will each customer use; once a provider is chosen, should its signature check be built; is the Outlook add-in needed?
62. **AI translation of customer lessons (ADR-066; ADR-008, questions 20 and 26).** When a Studio module is published, each lesson is translated by AI into every language of the organisation's language list that has no text yet: the lesson text the organisation wrote goes to the Anthropic API (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, low effort, a 2-minute timeout). A parity check protects ids, answers, targets and addresses, but the translations go live without a per-language human review: this narrows ADR-008's rule that AI material does not reach employees without approval. Privacy §5.1 and §6.3 name the AI subtitles and the Studio drafts sent to Anthropic, not the translation of the organisation's lessons on publish. The cap is 200 translation calls per organisation per day. In an organisation with ten languages one lesson means up to 9 calls, which run in parallel, and the publish button can wait up to 2 minutes. The subtitles use the cheaper tutor model. The form writes swipe (SMS only) and hotspot (email only) exercises. From you: do you approve AI translation of customer-written lessons and their publication without human review (if you do, the legal texts must cover it, question 26); should the daily cap of 200 and the model (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL` or the tutor model) stay; should the parallel calls be limited, or should translation move to a background job; which scene types beyond swipe and hotspot do the first customers need?
63. **Legal texts after wave C (ADR-067, continues question 26).** In ten languages the Privacy Policy and the Terms now say only what the code does: LDAP, Active Directory and SAML were removed, and sign-in is by email and password (at least 10 characters, pinned to `PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH` by a test) or by OpenID Connect; the row "Directory synchronisation reports: 180 days" was deleted from Privacy §8, AI Sel's questions and answers are kept up to 12 months and then deleted automatically, and §9 describes the isolation of organisations through the Service's own checks and an automated test suite, not RLS. This closes the two known mismatches in question 26 (RLS in §9, AI Sel's retention row). The edition headers did not change: Privacy v3, Terms v2, effective 2026-11-05, a date that has already passed. §6.2 says that the organisation's mail goes through its own mail server and mail that belongs to no organisation through the Provider's server; the mail of an organisation without a mail server, however, stays in the "logged" state and is never sent, and this is not written. The text in ten languages was written by an AI agent. From you or the lawyer: if publication waits for the lawyer, should the 20 edition headers and the 10 landing `consentVersion` values be raised together, or should v3/v2 and 2026-11-05 stay; do you confirm the deletion of the directory row; should §6.2 get a sentence for an organisation without a mail server; will SAML arrive before the text is published (question 14)? If it does, Terms 4.2 must name it again.
64. **The message for an unproven simulation sender (ADR-068).** When a simulation sender without a domain proof is saved, the administrator gets a message that names the domain: publish the TXT record on that domain, press "Check DNS", then save. The brief asked the message to point to the Identity tab (labelled "Sign-in" in the interface). The proof of the simulation domain, however, lives in the "Simulation sender" card of the Email tab, and the Sign-in tab has no domain proof, so the message names no tab and gives the steps of that card. From you: should it stay like this, or should the text name a tab (one string per language)?
65. **Purging the audit log and Privacy §8 (ADR-069, follow-up to question 48, ADR-055).** Privacy §8 says in ten languages that the audit log "cannot be changed or deleted through the Service" and is kept while the agreement is in force, and §9 calls it "append-only". Settings → Protection, however, lets an administrator choose a retention period for the audit log (ADR-048): `auditMonths` is 0 (keep everything) or at least 12 (ADR-055), and the daily clean-up job now applies the same 12-month minimum (`MIN_AUDIT_MONTHS`, ADR-069) and deletes older entries; the `settings.retention` and `retention.purged` entries are never deleted. The code cannot settle this conflict. From you: should the policy get a sentence in ten languages about the retention period the organisation chooses (never under 12 months), or should purging the audit log leave the Protection setting?
